guide.music_battle.panel.title: Panel and calibration
guide.music_battle.panel.keys: Open BM from the title or pause screen. Click a lane's key button, then press a key or mouse button to bind it. Esc cancels rebinding.
guide.music_battle.panel.speed: Note Speed changes how fast notes travel, from 0.5× to 20×. It does not change the music's tempo.
guide.music_battle.panel.skin: Choose bars, arrows, or circles for your notes. The preview shows the panel with your current settings.
guide.music_battle.panel.colors: Click a lane's color swatch to open the picker. Set each of the four lanes separately; the panel color does not change note colors. Other players see your note skin and colors.
guide.music_battle.panel.layout: Use the width, height, and opacity sliders to adjust the panel and lanes. Note size has separate controls. The preview updates as you change a setting.
guide.music_battle.npc.title: Custom opponent
guide.music_battle.npc.spawn: The Blocky Music Creative tab contains the TEST_RAP_GOD_MASTER spawn egg and its configuration wand. Use the egg on a block to place the NPC, then use the wand on it to open its settings.
guide.music_battle.npc.settings: Set the NPC's name and the username whose skin it should wear. Choose Classic or Slim arms, AI movement, invulnerability, glow, random voting, and whether the stationary NPC can be pushed. Use a microphone or Music Link to start a battle.
guide.music_battle.camera.recipe: To craft a camera, put an observer in the center, redstone above and below it, and iron ingots in the remaining slots.
screen.music_battle.dj_playlist.legacy_l: This set has more than 8 effects, so it opens in the extended list. Keep 8 or fewer to use the regular DJ menu.
guide.music_battle.calibration.title: Audio and input timing
guide.music_battle.calibration.audio: Open BM → Calibration. Watch the falling note and adjust Audio Offset until the click lines up with it crossing the line. Positive values delay sound; negative values play it earlier. The − and + buttons adjust by 1 ms.
guide.music_battle.calibration.input: After aligning audio, tap Space at the line at least 5 times, then choose Apply Measured Input Offset. Holding Space does not add more samples.
guide.music_battle.calibration.scope: Audio Offset applies in battles and in the editor. Input Offset adjusts input judgement separately from the audio.
guide.music_battle.colors: Click a color swatch to open the picker. The vertical strip chooses hue; the square adjusts saturation and brightness. Enter HEX or R, G, and B values for an exact match. Done keeps the color; Cancel restores the previous one.
guide.music_battle.object_outline: Object Outline traces block edges in the view. Set its color, thickness, opacity, and glow. Add palette colors and set the transition speed to cycle between them. Beat flashes, fade-in, and fade-out are supported.
guide.music_battle.hide_panels: Hide Battle Panels hides the panels above participants for the effect's duration.
guide.music_battle.hide_particles_hand: The Hiding effect has separate switches for particles, the first-person hand, and two types of HUD. Hide HUD removes Minecraft's hotbar, health, crosshair, and other HUD elements. Hide Blocky Music HUD removes participant panels on screen and above their heads, scores, track details, and battle prompts. You can enable both switches together. Menus and visual effects stay visible. The HUD returns when the effect ends, unless you hid it with F1.
guide.music_battle.camera.mouse: M switches between mouse-look and a free cursor. Rebind it in Blocky Music controls.
guide.music_battle.smiley.title: Smiley balls
guide.music_battle.smiley.spawn: The spawn egg creates a ball in a random color. Put a nether star in the center; red, orange, and yellow dyes across the top; lime and cyan on the sides; blue, purple, and magenta across the bottom.
guide.music_battle.smiley.dyes: Feed any dyes to two adult balls to breed them. To recolor a ball, hold Shift and use the desired dye on it. Balls cannot breed during a battle.
guide.music_battle.dj.playlist.title: Playlist and start position
guide.music_battle.dj.playlist.queue: Open the playlist, choose a track from the cover cards, and add it to the queue. You can add a track more than once. Use the arrows to reorder entries and Remove to delete the selected entry.
guide.music_battle.dj.playlist.cue: Select an entry and set its starting second in the time field or on its timeline. Enable Auto Advance to play the next entry when it ends.
guide.music_battle.dj.playlist.fx: Choose the entry's effect source: TRACK uses chart effects, DJ copies the booth's set, and NONE disables effects.
guide.music_battle.dj.fx.title: Effects and preview
guide.music_battle.dj.fx.edit: A DJ set holds up to 8 effects, including duplicates. Lower entries draw above earlier ones. Use the arrows to change the draw order. Chart FX and DJ FX have separate switches.
guide.music_battle.dj.fx.preview: Changes appear in the preview while you adjust an effect. Save keeps them; Cancel restores the settings from before editing. The Live monitor shows current chart and DJ effects through the selected camera.
guide.music_battle.dj.presets.title: Presets and reset
guide.music_battle.dj.presets.folder: Use the preset browser to save a named set, load it, or delete it. The files are in music_battle_dj_presets inside your game folder.
guide.music_battle.dj.presets.types: Visual FX presets save the effects and their settings. Equalizer presets store the three frequency bands. Audio presets include range, volume, EQ, and all audio effects.
guide.music_battle.dj.presets.reset: Reset Speakers restores a 14-block range, 100%% volume, and 0 dB on each EQ band. It affects the selected speaker or all speakers, depending on the panel mode.
guide.music_battle.preset_path: music_battle_dj_presets/ contains your DJ visual FX, audio, and equalizer presets.

music_battle.calibration.audio_help: Align the click with the note crossing the line. Positive values delay music relative to notes and FX; negative values play it earlier. The buttons adjust by 1 ms. Changes save immediately.
music_battle.calibration.input_help: This correction changes when the game judges your input. Positive values judge it earlier; negative values judge it later. Music, notes, and timing windows stay unchanged. Changes save immediately.

music_battle.l10n.guide.text_008: Craft a microphone: an iron ingot at the top, a copper ingot in the center, and a stick at the bottom.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_009: For solo play, hold Shift and right-click the air or a block with a microphone. Choose a track to combine P1 and P2 into one part.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_010: The BM button on the title and pause screens opens controls, audio, and panel settings.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_012: Right-click a player or mob with a microphone to challenge them. The microphone binds to you on first use and records your statistics.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_013: The volume slider adjusts music in battles and in the editor.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_016: Use a microphone on a player to send a challenge. They can accept or decline with the buttons in chat.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_017: Use a microphone on a mob, then choose a library and track in the voting screen.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_018: Solo play has no opponent or second panel. You can use x1.5 or x2 speed; solo results do not affect your duel statistics.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_019: Before starting, choose modifiers: shared notes, deadly party, x1.5/x2 speed, and mob difficulty.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_020: Whoever challenges a player or a mob chooses to be Player 1 or Player 2 when sending the challenge (Player 1 by default). If a chart contains only one player's part, both players play it; with two parts, Player 1 plays P1 and Player 2 plays P2.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_022: Press the four assigned keys when notes reach the hit line. Hold long notes until their tails end.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_023: During a musical break, Space votes to skip to the next section with notes. Participants can surrender from the Esc menu.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_024: Use your assigned gameplay keys during a battle. Esc opens the menu; other mod bindings and manual camera controls are disabled until the battle ends.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_027: Press V to watch a battle or DJ set through its selected camera. Press again to return to your usual view. Rebind it under Options → Controls → Blocky Music. Stay within listening range, which follows your character's position.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_028: The Spectator Effects setting completely disables track FX while you are not participating in a battle.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_031: Create New Track opens a blank chart. Edit opens an existing one, Create Copy duplicates it and its assets under a new ID, and Delete removes the local copy.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_032: The ID names the chart's folder and JSON file. Players see its title and description. Do not rename the folder or files by hand while the editor is open.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_034: Anyone can use the editor. Server publishing is available to operators and players granted access by an operator using /musicbattle publishaccess grant <player>.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_035: Publish sends the chart, music, and cover image to the current server.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_036: Preview images are saved as PNG, up to 1024 pixels on each side. If you choose a GIF, its first frame becomes the cover.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_037: The Published Tracks tab shows your uploads on this server and lets you remove them from the server.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_038: Custom charts may contain unwanted content. Open them only if you trust the author.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_041: music_battle_raw/ holds incoming OGG audio, images, and chart files available in the editor.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_042: music_battle_tracks/my_tracks/<id>/ contains the saved chart, music, and cover.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_044: saves/<world>/blocky_music/server_tracks/ holds server charts for a single-player world.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_045: saves/<world>/blocky_music/user_tracks/ holds charts published by players in this world. Dedicated servers use the same folders inside the world directory.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_047: Use Vorbis OGG files for music.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_048: Choose a PNG, JPG/JPEG, GIF, BMP, or WBMP cover image up to 64 MB.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_049: Import notes from Friday Night Funkin JSON, osu!mania .osu files, or .osz archives. Choose the difficulty you want from an .osz archive. Audio and backgrounds are copied too when available.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_051: Put your source files in music_battle_raw and select them with Audio, Image, and Chart. Save to create a complete chart with its assets in my_tracks.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_052: Back up the track folder before editing its JSON by hand.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_055: Enter the ID, title, description, and BPM. Audio, Image, and Chart cycle through matching files in music_battle_raw. Load reads the OGG, Play starts the music, and Save writes the chart.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_056: Click or drag the thin strip above the timeline to choose a playback position, then press Play. Game Preview shows the chart with gameplay panels and effects.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_058: Left-click an empty cell to place a tap note. Right-click to place a hold note or extend an existing hold. Left-click an existing note to select it, then press Delete to remove it.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_059: Left-drag a note to move it. Drag a hold note's edge to change its duration.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_060: Use the 1/4 grid for regular placement. The 1/8 grid adds a position between each pair of lines for finer timing.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_063: Use P1/P2 to choose the part you are editing. The other part's notes appear translucent. Both parts can have notes at the same time.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_064: Ctrl+left click adds or removes a note from the selection. Arrow keys move the selection through time and lanes. P1 ↔ P2 moves selected notes to the other player's part.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_065: Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+V pastes at the beginning of the current page, Delete removes the selection, Ctrl+Z undoes, and Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes. Clear Selection deselects everything.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_068: Scroll over the FX rows with the mouse wheel. There are 48 rows, with six visible at a time.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_069: Row 1 draws above the others, followed by rows 2–6, then 7–12, and so on. Several effects can share a row and run at the same time.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_072: Choose an effect and its settings in the FX Brush. Point places a short pulse, Length uses a set duration, and Range creates an effect between two clicks.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_073: Left-click an effect to open its settings; drag to move it or drag its edges to resize it. Right-click an occupied position to delete the effect. The grid, timeline, selection, copy, and undo work just as they do for notes.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_074: Hold the cursor over an effect for 3 seconds to read its settings.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_075: Choose the 1/4 or 1/8 grid for the timing precision you need.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_076: Ctrl+left click selects multiple FX. Arrow keys move them through time and rows. Clear Selection deselects them.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_078: Copy to Brush saves the selected effect's settings as a template. Apply Brush applies that template; for Text effects, the existing text is preserved.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_079: Enable Fade In and Fade Out separately and set their durations in ticks. Cover Text lets the effect affect text FX. Cover Interface puts it above gameplay panels. Turn off Cover Players or Cover Entities to keep those models visible above the effect.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_080: Use the FX editor's separate switches to turn off the default black bars and background dimming.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_081: In effect settings, Tab toggles full preview; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo parameter changes.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_084: Flash fires on the beat or fills the screen for the entire duration, with adjustable color, intensity, opacity, and softness.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_085: Old TV adds scanlines, fine noise, flicker, and a sweeping band. Each part has its own settings.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_086: Fish Eye sets lens curvature, radius, zoom, center, chromatic aberration, and edge darkening. Remove Black Edges stretches the image edges into empty areas caused by strong lens distortion.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_087: Cinematic Bars take independent top and bottom heights, frame offset, softness, shadow, and entrance animation.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_088: Shake offsets the camera and screen with adjustable amplitude.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_089: Pulse zooms the image to the beat. Link other effects to it to make them move together.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_090: Color Correction adjusts the entire frame's brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, gamma, and color temperature.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_092: Vignette darkens an adjustable area around the screen edges.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_094: Visualizer shows the playing music's frequencies as bars along an edge. Adjust its position, size, bar length, gradient, fill, and section count.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_095: Text draws a caption with selectable font, position, colors, outline, typing speed, and entrance and exit animations.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_096: Pixel Fire draws decorative flames along the bottom of the stage.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_097: Stars fills the screen with twinkling points. Choose base and highlight colors, size, density, center, spread, and brightness. Adjust twinkle and movement speed separately; a negative movement speed reverses direction.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_098: Player Highlight outlines participants, including armor and capes. Choose P1, P2, or both, then set colors, thickness, and glow. Spectators and mobs in range can have separate outline colors. Model Glow makes highlighted models ignore world lighting.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_100: Link an effect to Pulse to make it follow the pulse.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_101: Enable Cover Interface to draw an effect above gameplay panels. Disable Cover Text to keep text FX above it.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_104: Craft a Music Link from redstone, an ender pearl, and an amethyst shard. Use it on the first mob, then the second. Clicking a participant again cancels their current battle.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_105: Hold Shift when selecting mobs to configure their battle and difficulty before starting.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_107: Place a camera and right-click it to edit. With default controls, WASD moves it, Space and Shift change height, the mouse or arrow keys turn it, and Ctrl speeds up movement. The wheel changes the field of view (FOV). R resets position, rotation, and FOV to placement defaults. Enter or Esc saves.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_108: Control the active camera to change the view on air. To prepare another view, open a different camera with Control without pressing Select View.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_109: Place a camera near the arena or within range of any speaker relaying that battle's music.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_112: Speakers relay battle music and spectator effects. Right-click to set their range from 2 to 64 blocks, volume from 0 to 200%%, and equalizer. Bass, mids, and treble each range from −12 to +12 dB.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_113: Extend the sound by placing the next speaker within range of the previous source.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_114: Place a regular speaker anywhere in the crafting grid to make a horizontal one.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_115: Speaker recipe: iron in the corners and side slots, redstone at the top and bottom, and a note block in the center.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_117: Select several speakers and cameras with the wire, then use it once on a DJ panel. You can select the panel first instead: each following object connects immediately while the panel stays selected. The range is 64 blocks in the same dimension. Use an object again to remove it from the list. Shift + right-click a speaker to disconnect it; for a camera, select its DJ panel first. Shift + right-click the air to clear the selection.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_118: Click the DJ panel's Live monitor to open the gallery. Select a camera card and press Select View to switch the broadcast; Control opens its settings without switching.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_119: The camera must be in a loaded area for preview. Disable your Iris/Oculus shader pack to use the Live monitor.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_120: To direct battle views, place a DJ booth near the arena or within its speakers' coverage. Link cameras with a wire. Select View and the switch arrows change the participants' and spectators' camera.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_121: Edit the selected speaker or all connected speakers at once. Range, volume, and the three-band equalizer apply live without a save button.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_123: Choose tracks from the library on the left, or search by title above the cards. Play starts or resumes, Pause holds the current position, and Restart returns to the beginning. Click or drag the timeline to seek.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_124: The speed button cycles through x1, x1.5, and x2 without changing pitch.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_125: Choose the next track and press Download for Everyone to preload it for listeners within range of the booth and speakers. The current track may be playing or stopped.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_126: Set reverb, echo, and the low-pass filter in the audio tab. The master FX switch turns off processing.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_127: Open Visual FX to adjust the booth's effects. While a playlist entry with a DJ set plays, this menu edits that entry's effects.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_128: DJ panel recipe: a jukebox in the center, redstone in a cross, and iron ingots in the corners. Wire recipe: string in the center and redstone in a cross.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_130: /musicbattle tracks lists server charts and their locations.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_131: /musicbattle reload reloads the chart catalog; requires operator permissions.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_132: /musicbattle publishaccess grant <player> allows publishing; requires operator permissions.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_133: /musicbattle publishaccess revoke <player> revokes publishing permission; requires operator permissions.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_134: /musicbattle publishaccess check <player> checks publishing permission; requires operator permissions.
music_battle.l10n.guide.text_136: To add server charts, put complete track folders in blocky_music/server_tracks inside the world folder, then run /musicbattle reload.

screen.music_battle.workshop.wizard.acce: This takes a minute and you only do it once. You are responsible for everything you upload; when in doubt, ask the creators first. A QwU World account starts at 13, but publishing in the Workshop is for 16 and up.
Upload music, covers and charts you made, have permission for, or that a licence allows. Not sure? Publish without audio.

Mark strong language and adult themes in the lyrics, and charts whose effects flash more than three times per second. Covers and descriptions are seen by anyone browsing, with or without an account, so they must suit everyone aged 13 and up.
There are separate marks for AI-made audio, cover and charts. AI content is allowed once it is marked; an AI imitation of a real voice needs that person's permission.
Rights holders can have content removed. A removal after a copyright notice is a strike: two strikes stop uploads for 30 days, three end them. Strikes expire after 12 months.
Players and rights holders can report a map. Staff may ask for a fix, remove a part or sanction the account, always with a written reason you can appeal.
The Upload Rules, the Workshop Terms and the Content usage guide are the binding texts. These cards only summarise them.
